value.body: Motor Vehicle Inspectors work in a state's transport or motor vehicles department. They check vehicle fitness, conduct driving tests, inspect vehicles after accidents and enforce road-safety rules. Each state recruits for these posts, usually through its Public Service Commission.

items.label: Central minimum qualification
items.value: Class 10 + 3-year diploma in Automobile or Mechanical Engineering
items.note: Plus a driving licence for geared motorcycles and light motor vehicles; states add their own rules
items.source: MoRTH notification under Section 213(4), Motor Vehicles Act (as reported)

items.label: Who recruits
items.value: State PSC or state transport department

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Meet your state's recruitment rules: typically an Automobile or Mechanical engineering qualification, a valid driving licence and, in some states, one to two years of experience in an approved automobile workshop. Apply when the state notifies posts; selection is usually a written exam, sometimes followed by an interview.

value.title: At a glance
items: Recruitment is irregular and the rules differ from state to state.
Domicile and state-language requirements are common.
Work mixes office duties, driving tests and roadside enforcement.
